title: Human Reproductive System
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Taught with care and in the way the school decides (a female and a male teacher or the guidance counsellor). Use labelled diagrams, not photographs. Wording to be confirmed by a teacher. Questions are about body parts, changes and healthy coping, never about personal experience.

skills.key_step: The child names the parts of the male reproductive system (testes, scrotum, sperm duct, urethra, penis, glands) and what each does, keeping the urinary path apart.

floor.prerequisite: Can name organs and their jobs in a body system.
floor.question: What does the heart do?

representations: a matching card set: part, job
two coloured paths for sperm and urine
steps: Testes: make sperm; the scrotum holds them outside the body.
Urethra: carries urine or sperm out (not at the same time).
Penis: passes sperm and urine out of the body.

board.do: Draw the outline of the male system.
Label each part with its job.

misconceptions.repair: Testes make sperm; kidneys make urine.

misconceptions.ask: What else leaves through the urethra?
misconceptions.repair: The urethra carries urine or sperm.

listen_for: the testes are in the stomach
misconceptions.repair: The testes are in the scrotum, outside the body.

misconceptions.ask: Where does the sperm duct start?
misconceptions.repair: The sperm duct carries sperm from the testes.

checks.question: Which tube carries both urine and sperm out of the body, at different times?

skills.key_step: The child names the parts of the female reproductive system (ovaries, oviducts, uterus, cervix, vagina) and what each does, and places the uterus, not the stomach, as where a baby grows.

floor.prerequisite: Can name the male reproductive parts.
floor.question: Which part makes sperm?

representations: a calendar of a monthly cycle
steps: Ovaries: release eggs, about once a month.
Oviducts: carry the egg; fertilisation happens here.
Cervix: the neck of the uterus; the vagina leads outside.

board.do: Draw the outline of the female system.
Ask the child to label the ovaries and oviducts.

listen_for: the baby grows in the stomach
misconceptions.ask: Is the stomach part of the reproductive system?
misconceptions.repair: A baby grows in the uterus.
Ovaries release eggs; the uterus holds the baby.
The cervix is the neck of the uterus; the vagina opens outside.

misconceptions.ask: How long is a monthly cycle?

skills.key_step: The child describes physical changes in boys (voice breaks, shoulders broaden, body and facial hair, growth spurt) and girls (breasts, wider hips, periods, body hair, growth spurt), and knows they start at different ages for different people.

floor.prerequisite: Can name the male and female reproductive parts.
floor.question: Where does a baby grow?

representations: a two-column chart: boys, girls, both
a range of ages on a line (about 9 to 16)
steps: Both: growth spurt, body hair, pimples, sweat.
Boys: voice breaks, broader shoulders, facial hair.
Each person starts at their own time.
contexts: a class with learners of different heights

board.do: Draw three columns: boys, girls, both.

board.say: Name a change other than periods.

board.do: Ask the child to fill in the rest.

misconceptions.ask: Do girls also have a growth spurt?
misconceptions.repair: Both boys and girls change in adolescence.

misconceptions.ask: Do all learners in class have the same height?
misconceptions.repair: Changes start at different ages; that is normal.

misconceptions.ask: Is a period a normal part of growing up?
misconceptions.repair: Periods are normal, not an illness.

listen_for: girls do not change except periods
misconceptions.ask: What other changes happen in girls?
misconceptions.repair: Girls have many changes besides periods.

checks.question: Give one change in boys during adolescence.
checks.answer: voice breaks, facial hair, broader shoulders or a growth spurt

checks.question: Do all children begin adolescence at the same age?
checks.answer: No: each starts at their own time

skills.key_step: The child chooses healthy ways of coping with adolescence: wash daily with mild soap, change pads regularly and keep going to school, eat balanced meals, exercise, talk to a trusted adult, and avoid squeezing pimples.
representations: a chart: challenge, healthy way, unhealthy way
steps: Hygiene: wash daily; change pads every few hours.
Skin: wash gently; do not squeeze pimples.
Feelings: talk to a trusted adult.
Body: eat balanced meals and exercise.
contexts: a girl worried about missing school
a boy teased about his voice

board.say: What is a healthy thing to do?

board.do: Wait for "talk to a trusted adult".
Ask the child to add two more healthy ways.

misconceptions.ask: What happens to the skin after squeezing?
Who can you talk to at school?
How often should a pad be changed?
misconceptions.repair: Change pads regularly and keep going to school.

misconceptions.ask: What does a growing body need?

checks.question: Give one healthy way to cope with mood swings.
checks.answer: talk to a trusted adult, exercise, rest

checks.question: Why should a growing learner not skip meals?
checks.answer: the body needs food to grow
